The proposed ROSC employs current mode architecture that is different from conventional voltage mode architecture. This enables compact and fast switching speed to be achieved. By designing transistor sizes equally between one in a bias circuit and another in a voltage to current converter, the effect of process variation can be minimized. A prototype chip in a 0.18-μm CMOS demonstrated that the ROSC generates a stable clock frequency of 32.6 MHz within 1-μs start-up time. Measured line regulation and temperature coefficient were ±0.69% and ±0.38%, respectively.

articleTitle: PEVaS: Power and execution-time variation-aware scheduling for MPSoC
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: We propose a scheduling method with the consideration of both the Processing Element(PE) power consumption variation and the task execution time variation. Task allocation and scheduling (TAS) with the execution time and power consumption variation is necessary to obtain the feasible Multiprocessor System-on-Chip(MPSoC). For this issue, the previous method evaluates the yield of the execution time and power consumption after TAS. This method, however, may need large design time to satisfy the target yield due to too many iterations of TAS, or may not obtain any TAS satisfying the target yield. We propose a TAS method, called PEVaS, to achieve the minimum execution time with the combination of PEs that satisfies the power constraint with some probability. We show the result that PEVaS obtains three times larger margin of the execution time constraint with the same yield. Thus, we confirm the efficiency of the proposed method compared with that of the previous method, empirically.

articleTitle: Aperture error reduction technique for subrange SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: A novel aperture error reduction technique for subrange successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) is presented in this paper. By reusing capacitors of flash ADC during fine conversion phase, thermometer coarse capacitors belonging to CDAC can be removed from the circuit. Compared with the conventional subrange SAR ADC without front-end T/H, this technique can minimize aperture error effectively. The reduced number of sample capacitors also lowers the input capacitance. The proposed 11-bit 200Ms/s subrange SAR ADC, which consists of a 3.5-bit flash ADC for coarse conversion and an 8-bit SAR ADC for fine conversion is designed in a 65nm process with 1.2V power supply. Simulation results show that this design achieves 67.32dB SNDR and consumes 2.676mW.

articleTitle: Mixed-mode self-calibrated amplitude control scheme for MEMS vibratory gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: In this paper, a mixed-mode self-calibrated Automatic Gain Control (AGC) loop for MEMS applications is introduced. In MEMS-based vibratory gyroscope systems, an AGC is used to regulate the vibration amplitude of an inertia mass. Traditional analog AGCs suffer from a limited control range or bulky elements. Here, we present a low gain P-controller (Fine tuning) with digitally-controlled dynamic bias (Coarse tuning) for the AGC loop. The dynamic bias compensates for the low loop gain through the AGC and is generated using an error sense ADC. This approach achieves more than 9bits of uncalibrated oscillation amplitude accuracy over PVT without the need for trimming the gyroscope actuation gain. The power consumption of the designed main amplitude control circuitry is less than 200μW. The overall circuit was built using a standard 0.13μm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Low-power and low-noise fully differential difference amplifier for sub-nanoampere on-chip potentiostat
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: In this paper, we present a low-power, low-noise and wide dynamic range biosensor for neurotransmitter detection that exhibits high sensitivity and linearity. The design uses a fully differential difference amplifier (FDDA) to decrease the number of amplifiers in the control part, with reduced overall power consumption as a result. Moreover, this amplifier provides an output voltage swing that is almost twice that obtained with single-ended amplifiers. Finally, the two differential pairs at the FDDA input eliminate the need for impedance isolation buffers and matching resistors, consequently reducing system noise for improved sensitivity and accuracy. Designing this biosensor in 180 nm technology led to a current sensitivity of 900 fA, an input-referred noise of 6.9 µVrms and a power consumption of 53.9 µW.

articleTitle: 0.3–42.5 GHz wideband common emitter amplifier driver unit in 55 nm SiGe BiCMOS for 60 Gb/s silicon photonic Mach-Zehnder Modulator
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: A silicon integrated wideband common emitter amplifier driver unit in 55 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology designed for a 60 Gb/s silicon photonic segmented Mach-Zehnder Modulator (SE-MZM) is reported in this paper. It achieves a bandwidth of 42.2 GHz (0.3-42.5 GHz), allowing the transmission of an On-Off Keying (OOK) modulated optical signal on a single optical channel with a data rate of up to 60 Gb/s. For a power consumption of 125 mW, it provides a small signal gain of 18 dB and a single-ended peak-to-peak output voltage swing of up to 1.1 V on a 50 Ω output load. The die active area is as small as 204 × 137 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 180 GHz frequency multiplier in a 130nm SiGe BiCMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: An integrated analog frequency multiplier for a novel high data rate communication system has been developed to multiply a 18GHz input signal by ten to generate a 180 GHz output signal. With a first step the 18GHz input signal is fed into a times five edge combiner, which generates an intermediate frequency of 90 GHz. Therefore five different phases with a delta of 72 degree are needed, that are provided by an active allpass filter chain. In a second step the 90 GHz intermediate frequency is given into a double-balanced Gilbert cell mixer. Here, frequency doubling is achieved by feeding the same signal into the LO and RF port of the mixer. Hence, the overall output frequency of 180GHz results in 180 GHz with a simulated output power of -7 dBm. All simulations are done post-layout. The chip is implemented in a 130nm BiCMOS technology with a chip area of 0.9mm × 1 mm.

Author Keywords: simultaneous phase and amplitude regenerative sampling

articleTitle: Innovative device source/drain and channel implantation for MOS transistors in ultra low power subthreshold circuit applications
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a new comprehensive doping scheme for the transistors in subthreshold circuits. The proposed doping is characterized by the absence of halos at the source and drain ends. We propose a Gaussian doping distribution inside the source and drain regions, and a low-high-low distribution across the depth of the transistor from the channel surface towards the body region. It also has a low-high-low doping distribution along the length of the transistor below the channel region. The analysis is performed by changing the doping densities, body bias and gate-source voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</sub>) to observe the variations of off-current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub>), threshold voltage and I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub> ratio. Results show that the optimized device with the proposed doping profile would provide higher drain current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>) and I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</sub> at a certain body bias.

articleTitle: A digitally programmable 50–150dB DC gain operational transconductance amplifier in 130nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an operational transconductance amplifier for closed-loop operation with extremely high DC gain and large gain-bandwidth product. The design principle is based on the cascade of undamped integrators to realize large DC gains and a controller to stabilize its operation in a closed-loop configuration. With a predetermined set of numbers, the OTA can be programmed into different states to realize various transfer functions and system orders. Gaussian transfer function is implemented as an example in this work. The chip is fabricated in the IBM 130 nm CMOS process, and measured data reveals DC gains ranging from 50 to 150 dB with a minimum 3-dB bandwidth of 10 kHz and a unity gain frequency of 10 MHz. This design principle is general and can be applied to any type of circuit technology in integrated or discrete implementation.

articleTitle: An evaluation framework of OS-level power managements for the big.LITTLE architecture
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: The big.LITTLE architecture, that is single-ISA heterogeneous multi-core, has been attracted attention as a modern processor architecture. Appropriate power management methods can achieve high-performance and power-efficiency of embedded real-time systems simultaneously. This paper proposes an evaluation framework of OS-level power managements for the big.LITTLE architecture. The proposed framework is designed as a Linux process which consists of the evaluation tool and power management plug-ins. We define the specification of interfaces on the evaluation tool regarding the application and Linux kernel for the portability. Actual value of energy consumption for a real-time task set can be measured by the scheduler and the power management module. We demonstrate the practicality of the framework by implementing it onto ODROID-XU3. Embedded system designers come to explore and discuss which is the most energy-efficient method for their target system by considering the actual measurement value.

articleTitle: A 77.1dB/108.9dB SNDR dual-mode delta-sigma modulator
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-mode delta-sigma modulator. The modulator can be configured for two structures, 3rd-order 4-bit in low-frequency high-resolution applications, and 2nd-order 4-bit in high-frequency low-resolution applications. Most of the circuit parts including the capacitors and switches are shared in both modes. An efficient OTA and comparators with Input Offset Calibration technique are adopted. The modulator is fabricated in 180nm CMOS technology. It achieves 77.1dB and 108.9dB peak Signal to Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR) separately in two modes with 1.25MHz and 39kHz input signal bandwidth. The power consumption is about 12mW.

articleTitle: Parallel hybrid bispectrum-multiframe blind deconvolution algorithm for horizontal imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a massively parallel hybrid, bispectrum speckle imaging (SI) and multi-frame blind deconvolution (B-MFBD) image reconstruction technique for anisoplanatic, long horizontal path imaging. We use a fast initial estimate, generated using parallel bispectrum SI technique, to initialize the parallel multi-frame blind deconvolution (MFBD) algorithm. The proposed hybrid B-MFBD technique, through massive parallelization, significantly speedups both existing iterative bispectrum SI and MFBD parts of the hybrid algorithm. We report a speedup factor of 7.31 with respect to sequential implementation of the same algorithm for an image size of 256 × 256.

articleTitle: Low emission, open loop MAC protocol compliant implantable FSK modulator
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: The current paper proposes a low emission media access control (MAC) compliant frequency shift keying modulator to operate within wireless body area networks (WBANs). Frequency modulation is achieved by utilizing a ramp to encode the bit stream into two distinct frequencies. The negotiated frequency of operation for dynamic frequency shifting and frequency encoding is achieved changing the gradient of the ramp thorough load cap and charging current in a charge pump. A tent map chaotic map has been utilized to module the signal resulting in lowering EMI Emissions. The work has been implemented on 0.18μm AMS technology and silicon measurement results presented.

articleTitle: An ULP and very efficient adaptively biased LDO regulator for harvesting application
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low power (ULP), low quiescent current, low-dropout regulator with a class-AB and an adaptively biased error amplifier (EA). The high slew rate (SR) and the closed loop bandwidth improve the regulator transient response. Adapting the quiescent current regarding the transient response permits a high current efficiency at steady state. The stability is ensured for the entire output current range (1 μA - 3 mA) and for a maximum output capacitor of 100 pF by the current buffer compensation technique and the standard Miller capacitor compensation. The output voltage is set to 0.8 V with a minimum supply voltage of 0.92 V and a maximum quiescent current of 3.2 μA.

articleTitle: Design of pulse synthesizers for the convergence of IR-UWB solutions
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents some techniques to synthesize pulses in the context of IR-UWB. Pulse synthesizers are good candidates when different kinds of pulses are needed to comply with different standards or when the shape of the pulses needs to be modified. Two different approaches are described here. Voltage Controlled Delay Line (VCDL) based pulses are first described. For this family, two kinds of combiners are presented: differential pairs based and H-bridge based. The second one achieves a larger output dynamic but is limited by the use of the VCDL. A second type of H-bridge based synthesizer using VCO is presented. Using both a VCO and a H-Bridge offers the largest synthesis capabilities since it allows large voltage pulses to be synthesized and the pulse duration is not limited. All proposed architectures have been implemented and their measured performances are given for comparison.

articleTitle: A palmtop platform for miniaturized dielectric spectroscopy from MHz to GHz
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a self-sustained, palmtop, measurement platform for miniaturized dielectric spectroscopy (DS) from MHz to GHz. It incorporates a microfluidic DS sensor, a fully integrated transceiver (TRX) IC, a Raspberry Pi as a low-cost, embedded computing module, and a handheld tablet for wireless display and platform operation control. With dimensions of 10cm × 6.5cm × 5.5cm and weight of 295g, the platform is small enough to fit on the palm of a hand, and accurately measures both the real and imaginary parts of the complex relative dielectric permittivity, ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>, of a material-under-test (MUT) from ~ 9MHz to 2.4GHz. The platform is capable of differentiating among de-ionized (DI) water, lemonade, red wine, and vodka as primarily-water-based MUTs at four different excitation frequencies of 33MHz, 487MHz, 1.087GHz, and 2.177GHz. Moreover, dielectric readings of the platform with mixtures of DI water and different concentrations of ethanol at 32 frequency points in ~ 10MHz-2.4GHz show excellent agreement with those from bulk-solution reference measurements by a benchtop Agilent 85070E dielectric probe interfaced with a vector network analyzer (VNA) equipment.

articleTitle: A phasor-domain study of injection-locking of harmonic oscillators with multiple injections
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a phasor-domain study of injection-locking of harmonic oscillators under multiple injections with the consideration of the effect of the nonlinear characteristics of the oscillators. The relation between lock range, oscillation condition, and the nonlinear characteristics of oscillators is obtained. The lock range of oscillators under multiple injections and that under a single injection are also obtained. We show that harmonic oscillators with harsh nonlinearities exhibit a larger lock range. We further show that harmonic oscillators with multiple injections exhibit a larger lock range as compared with those with single injection. The maximum lock range of oscillators with dual injections is twice that with a single injection. The theoretical findings are verified using the simulation results of LC oscillators designed in IBM 130 nm 1.2 V CMOS technology.

articleTitle: A half-rate 100 Gb/s injection-locked clock/data recovery circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: A 100 Gb/s clock/data recovery circuit using a high-speed BiCMOS process is designed and simulated. In this circuit a half-rate 50 GHz clock signal, injected in parallel with the tail current of an LC VCO, locks to a 100 Gb/s input NRZ data signal. Inductive tuning for the frequency tuning of the VCO is employed, which gives a wide frequency tuning range while maintaining a constant quality factor.

articleTitle: A dual Gm-mode LC-tank VCO with programmable-in-size-and-current active core and pseudo-exponential tank capacitance
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: An LC-tank quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QVCO) with an octave overall tuning range is designed and fabricated in AMS 0.35μm 2P/4M RF CMOS. The VCO utilizes an nMOS-based, cross-coupled, programmable-in-size-and-current active core for dual G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-mode operation to overcome a tradeoff between the VCO minimum frequency limited by the startup gain of its active core and the VCO maximum frequency impacted by parasitic capacitances of the active core. The VCO also employs a pseudo-exponential tank capacitance with both coarse and fine tuning, which highly linearizes the coarse-tuning characteristics and reduces the variation of the VCO gain factor across the tuning range. The VCO achieves 66.3% frequency-tuning range (FTR) from 1.232 to 2.455GHz with measured phase noise of -119.5 and -121.5dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from the minimum and maximum oscillation frequencies, respectively. The measured power consumption is 6mW at 2.455GHz and 15mW at 1.232GHz from 1.5V.

articleTitle: Tracking BTI and HCI effects at circuit-level in adaptive systems
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This work proposes a new method for measuring the performance loss of a processor due to aging (BTI and HCI). It is designed for any adaptive system incorporating in-situ delay monitors and local temperature sensors. To validate it, we developed a simplified circuit-level model for BTI/HCI effects in 28nm FD-SOI technology with a relative small error (<;1%). The correct operation of the proposed method has been verified in MATLAB/Simulink environment. It is shown that one can measure the circuit aging over a wide range of temperatures, the circuit aging being determined by the reduction of the maximum clock frequency.

articleTitle: An 11-bit 200MS/s subrange SAR ADC with charge-compensation-based reference buffer
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an 11-bit 200MS/s subrange SAR ADC with charge-compensation-based (CCB) reference buffer. The precision, stability and noise of reference voltage are critical to the performance of ADC. Charge is released to or absorbed from reference during data conversion, resulting in fluctuation of reference voltage. Conventionally a large on-chip decoupling capacitor is required to stabilize reference voltage. In this paper, charge losing of reference for a subrange SAR ADC is analyzed, and a charge-compensation-based reference buffer is designed to reduce decoupling capacitor size. The implemented ADC was measured with the charge compensation circuit disabled and enabled, respectively. Measurement results show obvious improvement on SFDR and SNDR with reference charge-compensated.

articleTitle: On lossy memristive behavior of metal conductors
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: The memristive behavior of metal conductors is considered and the question as to whether or not it can be observed in a common copper wire is answered. Mathematical modeling techniques and simulation results are presented to confirm our hypothesis that at excitation frequencies related to the thermal time constant of the wire, pinched hysteresis curves can be observed and a metal conductor is therefore a memristor.

articleTitle: On design of memory retention LDO regulator
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: The paper describes operation and design of a memory retention LDO regulator. The LDO regulator is operating in a very wide range of the output currents (up to 100 uA) with a very small quiescent current (in the range of 100-300 nA). In the proposed circuit this range is achieved using a nonlinear translinear cell added to the the unity gain stage (voltage follower). The cell provides the load controlled bias current in the main loop. The regulator is inherently stable: the translinear cell operates outside the gain loop. Even it is not required in memory retention applications, this LDO regulator can provide a fast load step response. The circuit was designed for 130 nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Top-down design and synthesis of inherently-stable integrator-based high-order amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: A defined, straightforward top-down design method is proposed for developing inherently-stable, fast-settling high-order amplifiers. The method effectively defines the closed-loop response for a multistage amplifier through a desirable transfer function, such as of a time-domain filter, and combines an efficient g<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-based procedure to implement a compact corresponding CMOS circuit. The amplifier will be composed of a cascade of g<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>-C integrators to supply the dc gain, followed by a stabilizing controller. Hence, several gain stages, more than the typical three, can be employed to build high-order structures that can achieve ultra-high gain. In support of the proposed approach, a four-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with a third-order modified-Bessel unity-gain feedback response is implemented in 0.13-μm CMOS. Simulation results demonstrate that the OTA achieves a dc gain of 78 dB and realizes the anticipated, pre-defined closed-loop response while driving a 1-pF capacitive load.

articleTitle: SMASH-MASH delta-sigma modulator using noise-shaping quantizers
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: In this paper, a new multi-loop delta-sigma modulator is proposed. The proposed modulator combines the use or digital filters in a multi-stage noise-shaping (MASH) structure with an in-loop digital addition or Sturdy-MASH (SMASH) modulators. This structure works with any types or modulator loops and quantizers and integrates exceptionally well with noise-shaping quantizers where the traditional SMASH Tails. Furthermore, the proposed modulator relaxes the critical analog/digital matching problem or the MASH modulators while providing excellent stability. Simulation results and mathematical analysis are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness or the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Design of a DCO based on worst-case delay of a self-timed counter and a digitally controllable delay path
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: Delay path reconfiguration is used to control frequency output in Digitally Controlled Oscillators. In order to achieve a very low frequency range, if the delay path is not properly designed, this would result in large area overhead and leakage power loss. An alternative delay path is proposed for the DCO, based on a unit delay as the smallest possible delay, with added architecture to multiply the unit delay using digital control bits, this allows the delay output to be near-linear. The proposed delay path has two control modes, a 2-bits fine grain control and 6-bit coarse control. Simulation results show that the frequency of the DCO ranges from 34.92MHz to 448MHZ at 1.1V with maximum average power consumption of 358.27μW at 1.1V.

articleTitle: A charge-pump based multi-mode stimuli generator for cardiac pacemaking
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: A multi-mode charge pump based stimulator for cardiac pacemaking is presented. This system operates both as voltage-mode and charge-mode stimulator and can deliver voltage stimulus to the tissue with an arbitrary waveform. The core of the stimulator is a reconflgurable 3-stage charge pump circuit with variable switching frequency allowing to adjust the stimulus level to the desired value in a wide range. Two output stage switches control the connection of the charge pump to the load and determine the stimulation mode. If the charge pump output is always connected to the load, the voltage-mode stimulation will be realized whereas in the charge-mode stimulation, first a capacitor is charged to a specific voltage by the charge pump and then the controlled amount of charge is injected from the capacitor to the load while the charge pump has been disconnected. The measurements performed making use of a prototype PCB show that the systems can inject charge to the load in the range of 5 to 29 nC in the charge-mode and generates voltage pulses with the amplitude varies between 2.63 and 11.4 V in the voltage-mode stimulation. The stimulator efficiency varies from 65 to 90% for different output voltage stimulation levels.

articleTitle: A low-cost camera-based transducer tracking system for freehand three-dimensional ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: Freehand three-dimensional ultrasound (3D US) imaging is commonly used for various diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. In this technique, accurate tracking of the US transducer is a crucial requirement to develop high-quality 3D US volumes. However, current methods for transducer tracking are generally expensive and inconvenient. This paper presents a low-cost camera-based system for tracking the US transducer with six degrees of freedom (DoF). In this system, two orthogonal cameras with non-overlapped views are mounted on the US transducer. During US scanning, the two cameras are employed to track artificial features attached to the skin of the patient. A 3D surface map is constructed based on the tracked features and the 3D poses of each camera with respect to the skin are extracted separately. The estimated poses of the two cameras are spatially combined to provide accurate and robust pose estimation of the US transducer. The camera-based tracking of the US transducer has been applied to synthesize freehand 3D US volumes. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated by performing in-vitro 3D US imaging experiments and quantifying the synthesized US volumes. The results demonstrate that two points in the 3D US volume separated by a distance of 10 mm can be reconstructed with an average error of 0.7 mm.

articleTitle: Improving placement algorithms by using visualization tools
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: EDA tools paved the way for the integration of billion of components in a single integrated circuit. However, many tools still rely on text interfaces. The use of visualizations tools can help not only to provide a visual output of an EDA tool but also to show how a tool is performing in terms of quality of results. A good graphic output can be useful to improve algorithms or develop new ones. Some placement visualization tools are shown and it is provided a perspective how these visualization tools contributed to the improvement and development of new algorithms developed by us.

articleTitle: 0.18-µm CMOS driver optimization for maximum data rate under power and area constraints
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a Mach-Zehnder-based transmitter in 0.18 μm CMOS. An asymmetric driver is proposed to achieve a large output swing on the optical modulator. The logical effort method was applied on each driver block in order to optimize the propagation delay. The driver characteristics are analyzed based on slew-rate limitation. The speed-power-area trade-off is highlighted and enables to adjust the driver design according to specified constraints. Driver performance obtained with early-design-stage equations is compared to post-layout simulations. Good agreement is demonstrated which validates the proposed sizing methodology.

articleTitle: Byte-Based Partial-Match instruction and data compression for high-performance and low-power interconnects
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: With improvement in technology, the number of cores and the numbers of threads per core keep increasing. As a result, instruction and data transferred on interconnects increase significantly. Interconnects are becoming a performance and power bottleneck of multi-core systems. In this paper, we present our compression scheme, Byte-Based Partial-Match (PM) compression for both instruction and data transferred at all memory levels. Our simulation results show that, on average, about 28%~67% compression ratios can be achieved with PM compression. Overall performance of a system can be increased by 1.4%~21.9% with default system bus widths. With compressed bus widths, about 7%~40% of interconnect power can be saved.

articleTitle: Data transient insensitive phase-locked loops
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a comparable study of the locking characteristics of phase-locked loops (PLLs) with an integrating bang-bang phase detector with that of PLLs with an Alexander full-rate bang-bang phase detector. Both periodic and single-event data transients are used to investigate the lock performance of two PLLs with identical configuration and components but different phase detectors. Simulation results demonstrate that PLL with a full-rate Alexander bang-bang phase detector fails to lock when incoming data stream is corrupted with data transients whereas that with an integrating bang-bang phase detector successfully establishes lock.

articleTitle: A modified RNS-to-binary converter scheme for {22n+1 − 1, 22n+1, 22n − 1} moduli set
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an area efficient adder based reverse converter for a recently proposed new moduli set {2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup> - 1, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup>, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</sup> - 1}. First, we simplify the New Chinese Remainder Theorem (New CRT I) to obtain a reverse converter. Second, we further reduce the resulting architecture to obtain a memoryless reverse converter that uses three 2n bits CSAs (CSA1, CSA2, CSA3), two parallel CPAs (2n + 1-bit CPA1 and 2n-bit CPA2) and 4n+1-bit CPA3. From the theoretical results our proposal utilizes (10n+4)FA and (4n-2)HA area resources with a conversion time of (6n+5)t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FA</sub>+t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MUX</sub>, where CSA, CPA, FA, HA, t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FA</sub>, and t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MUX</sub> denote respectively, Carry Save Adder, Carry Propagate Adder, Full adder, Half Adder, the delay of one full adder and that of a multiplexer. Experimental result which is the ultimate contradicts the theoretical result and suggests that the area resource requirements of our proposal is reduced by 33.7% at the expense of 20.9% more conversion time required for our converter when compared with the state of the art.

articleTitle: Improved alias rejection using interleaved CIC decimation filter
publicationTitle: 2016 14th IEEE International New Circuits and Systems Conference (NEWCAS)
abstract: Decimation filter for sampling rate alteration in sigma delta converters is generally designed using cascaded integrator comb CIC structure. The frequency response of the structure is sinc function that exhibits poor stop band characteristics which thereby require additional compensation filter stages. This paper presents two-way interleaved multistage CIC structures for even decimation factors. Among the two proposed multistage structures, one consists of CIC in interleaved form as first stage and non-recursive form as second stage while the other structure has both the stages realized in interleaved form. The cascaded two stage interleaved structure shows better rejection for second and third aliasing bands with increased delay elements. These interleaved filters provide twice increase in alias rejection for every linear increase in order without using any compensation stages. The stop band attenuation for these filters is improved by 2-20 dB than classical CIC filter of corresponding order.
